newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower as blue chips slide.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower as blue chips slide.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip issues took a battering on Thursday dragged down by Telekom, before staging a mild recovery in late afternoon,
At the close the key Composite Index of 100 leading blue-chip stocks fell 7.84 points, or 0.71 percent, to 1,100.41. It had fallen to a low of 1,088.56 earlier.
Telekom fell to a low of 11.40 ringgit in late afternoon, before recovering to finish unchanged at 12.20 ringgit.
"The market is feeling a bit bearish about (Telekom's) Thai venture," said Greg Feldberg, telecommunications analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Kuala Lumpur.
Telekom said earlier in the week it had bought a 20.12 percent stake in Thai telecommunications firm Samart.
Feldberg also pointed to concerns over the impact of earlier-than-expected local deregulation within the telecommunications market as a major concern over the stock.
Telekom contributes around 10 percent of the weighting of the Composite Index.
"The focus is on selling index-linked stocks and situationals on the second board," said Patrick Zecha, head of research at South Johor Securities.

Time Engineering extended its fall, losing six cents to 4.10. Time said on Wednesday it may delay listing its Time Telecommunications unit due to soft market conditions, a move which analysts said would delay the injection of new funds needed to expand its infrastructure.
Bakun dam developer Ekran ended unchanged at 5.50 ringgit after earlier falling as much as 25 cents on requotation, following its poorly received rights issue.
Other companies controlled by Ekran's executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing were mixed.
Property developer and industrial concern Wembley jumped 50 cents to 4.30, and timber and property firm Granite rose 12 to 3.72.
Engineering firm PWE Industries fell 1.0 ringgit to 36.75, and timber firm Pacific Chemical was off 5.0 cents to 6.10.
Banking stocks were easier on some concerns that Ekran's flopped rights issue may ripple to other big share issues which are underwritten by merchant banks, analysts said.
Commerce Asset-Holdings Bhd fell five cents to 7.15, Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank by 40 to 16.60, Maybank by 50 to 26.50 and DCB Holdings by five to 8.30.
